name: Meningeal Melanocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Meningeal Melanocytoma

criteria.description: Presence of pigmented spindle or epithelioid melanocytic cells with low mitotic activity on histopathological examination
MRI showing well-circumscribed, extra-axial mass with T1 hyperintensity and T2 hypointensity consistent with melanin content
Positive immunostaining for melanocytic markers such as HMB-45, Melan-A, and S-100 protein
Neurological symptoms related to mass effect depending on tumor location

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with positive melanocytic immunohistochemistry and compatible MRI findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from malignant melanoma and other pigmented meningeal tumors is critical

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits correlating with tumor location

searchTerms: epileptic episodes due to brain lesion

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Visual disturbances from optic pathway involvement
searchTerms: seeing disturbances related to optic pathway
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems
loss of coordination from cerebellar pressure
balance problems due to brain compression

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: vomiting caused by increased intracranial pressure

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss if tumor involves auditory pathways
searchTerms: hearing loss from tumor near ear nerves

occasional.symptomName: Neck stiffness or meningeal irritation signs

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus due to CSF flow obstruction
Spinal cord compression symptoms if tumor is spinal
Melanotic skin lesions associated with neurocutaneous melanosis

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or shows mild protein elevation without malignant cells
imaging: MRI: well-circumscribed extra-axial mass with T1 hyperintensity and T2 hypointensity due to melanin
CT: hyperdense lesion with possible calcifications
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; BRAF mutations rare compared to malignant melanoma
other: Histopathology: pigmented spindle or epithelioid melanocytes with low mitotic index
Immunohistochemistry: positive for HMB-45, Melan-A, S-100

distinguishingFeatures: High mitotic activity and cellular atypia on histology
More aggressive clinical course with metastases
Different immunohistochemical profile (EMA positive, melanocytic markers negative)
Typical imaging features without T1 hyperintensity

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
New onset seizures or focal neurological deficits
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Kleinschmidt-DeMasters BK, et al. Meningeal melanocytoma: a clinicopathologic study of 14 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2000.
Orphanet: Meningeal melanocytoma. Orphanet Report Series, 2023.
